notes: ROUTED HERE BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-22 16:05Z. He was shown the eleven marks and the constraints below and answered "defer to chatgpt". So this is not a request for approval of a drawing; it is a request to rule on whether the reading these marks would give a player is the right one, before anybody draws anything.

WHAT IS BUILT AND REACHED TODAY. src/player/PersonCard.tsx renders another person's temperament at data-testid="person-card-traits": observedTraitLabels() joins the words with a middle dot, so a person reads as "Reserved · Thinks it through · Takes chances". It is shown for other people only, never for the character being played. So a person's whole character is five plain words in the same type as everything else on the card.

THE TEN POLES, AS THE CODE HAS THEM. Reserved / Outgoing; Thinks it through / Acts on impulse; Conciliatory / Confrontational; Lets things slip / Follows through; Cautious / Takes chances. Plus "Neither, much", which a person genuinely holds and which is not an absence.

THE CONSTRAINTS THIS LANE PUT ON THE ART, EACH OF WHICH IS A DESIGN CLAIM RATHER THAN A DRAWING PREFERENCE, AND ANY OF WHICH THE DIRECTOR MAY OVERRULE. (1) No pair may read as a good end and a bad end: shown the pair without the words, a player should not be able to say which end the game approves of. (2) Nothing may read as a measurement — no scale, dial, meter, bar, star, tick, or filled-versus-empty pair — because these are behavior tendencies and the game never reports them as a quantity. (3) No lettering, initials or numerals, since every word in this game is generated per world. (4) No faces, which would contradict the portrait beside the line. (5) One flat tintable color, legible at body-text size on a phone.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH, AND MUST NOT. How fast a personality changes rides PersonalityTendencyRecord.strength, per the owner's settled ruling that the pace depends on how strongly that person holds the trait. These marks say what somebody is like and never how much, so nothing here reintroduces a fixed band per trait name.

INVENTORY, READ BEFORE FILING. All 126 assets in art/manifest/asset_manifest.json searched by asset_id and asset_type for trait, personality, temperament, icon, glyph, badge, symbol and mark. Every match is a character layer or one of the two seated candidate renders. There is no interface glyph of any kind in the project. The nearest existing request, ui-shell-reference-icons, is a different set — five navigation icons for the pin rail — and is named as the style authority rather than duplicated.
The request itself is art/requests/asset-requests.json, requestId ui-temperament-marks-ten-poles, filed at P2 and reconciled as unaffected-still-required.
question: (1) Is a mark per pole the right way to make a person's character legible on their card, or does a small drawing beside a plain word add noise rather than reading? (2) Are the five temperaments the right five to show a player at all, given that what a player needs from somebody else's card is a guess at how they will behave? (3) Does the no-good-end rule hold for every pair, or is there a pair where the game honestly should let a player read one end as harder to deal with — confrontational, or lets things slip? (4) Is "Neither, much" worth its own mark, or is a person who holds no strong tendency better shown by the word alone with no mark beside it? (5) Should the marks appear for a person a player barely knows, or only once the player has seen enough of them to have earned the reading — the game already distinguishes what is observed from what is true.

title: Whether a mark per temperament pole is the right way to show what somebody is like
usableAnswer: A yes or no on the mark-per-pole idea, and if yes, a ruling on each of the four constraints this lane invented — in particular whether every pair must read as neutral. A position on whether the marks are earned or immediate. No drawing, no color and no file format is being asked for here; the art request already carries those.
whyItMatters: The mind layer is the thing the owner ranks at 1A, and the one surface a player actually reads it on renders it as the least visible line on the card. Either a mark fixes that or the line needs a different treatment, and drawing eleven of the wrong thing is the expensive way to find out.

answer.summary:
Use plain, prominent, short observed descriptors first. Optional small symbols may reinforce those words, but are not required for the behavior or card to ship and must not become an eleven-icon neutral/pole checklist. Keep the five underlying dimensions, and surface relevant known named traits as breadth arrives. 'Neither, much' need not occupy a dedicated symbol slot; balanced is not unknown, and unknown must not be displayed as balanced.

Show another person's descriptor only when justified by observation or legitimate information, using the existing observed/actual distinction. An early impression can be qualified and later revised. No meter/star/rating that suggests measured reliability. No universal green good/red bad moral classification. However, the text may honestly explain that unreliable follow-through matters for a specific commitment; a no-good-end art constraint does not abolish consequences.

The requested symbols remain optional candidates for existing art review, not automatic approval or an excuse to delay people depth. Do not put letters/numbers into generated image assets to encode facts; text is rendered by the interface, independent of the asset. These choices change presentation only, not personality-change intensity or the person's underlying traits.

Acceptance ChatGPT requests (not executed): A new acquaintance shows only an appropriately tentative known impression; repeated card opens reveal nothing new. A later contradiction can revise the impression. Plain text remains fully understandable with symbols absent.
